title: “superVisionPJ”: Opportunities and Limitations of Group Supervision in the Context of Clinical Training (Final Year) as Part of Medical Professional Development
summary:
Background:
For decades, studies from around the world have shown that medical students often experience high levels of stress during their studies. Mental health issues are more common among them than in the general population or among students in other fields of study. The clinical year (in Germany called "Praktisches Jahr" (PJ))—the final stage before the state examination—is a particularly stressful phase. International and national findings confirm that future physicians face major structural and personal challenges during this time. In Germany, there have been very few group programs designed specifically to help students in the clinical year discuss these professional and personal stresses together and find solutions. For this reason, the Department of Palliative Medicine at the University Medical Center Freiburg, in collaboration with the Office of the Dean of Studies at the Faculty of Medicine, is offering the pilot project “superVisionPJ.” This specialized group program will be evaluated as part of a concurrent scientific study.

Research questions:
How do the participating PJ students experience group supervision? What opportunities and limitations do they perceive in this context?
In addition, the broader context will be examined: How does the group evaluate their experiences and the challenges of the clinical internship as an important step on the path to becoming a physician? To what extent can the group supervision program support this process?


Study Design:
This is a qualitative study. This means that no numerical values are measured; instead, experiences are collected. To this end, group discussions, individual interviews (in which participants are free to report on their experiences), and a short questionnaire on personal data are used. The discussions are recorded and transcribed verbatim.
The group discussions are analyzed using two different methods: First, the content is summarized in a structured manner. Second, (provided the participants’ responses are sufficiently diverse) the study examines which common and differing patterns of thought and orientation exist within the group.
The individual interviews are also analyzed for content. In doing so, close attention is paid to the language used and the underlying meanings of the statements.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All internal medicine clinical year students at the University Medical Center Freiburg,
•    who have participated in group supervision and who wish to participate in the qualitative study on a voluntary and informed basis, and
•    who have already been in their clinical year for at least 4 weeks at the time of the survey.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe psychological distress (e.g., severe
depression, suicidal ideation, psychosis) that prevents participation in the study
